done.why: I had read the one strong scene, the duel with the hooded figure. The rest of the map I saw was sparse, so I stopped with most exits unexplored.

about: A sequel-style cave adventure. You arrive at the bottom of a stair as the bearer of an old lantern. In the Land of Shadow you meet a hooded figure with a glowing sword like yours, who mirrors you and fights like a teacher. It reads as a test of the self.

ending.what: I defeated the shadow figure and it vanished. I did not find the old man or reach a final ending.

moments.note: The sword description, 'a hilt worn to the shape of a hand... turns out to be yours', is a lovely line.
The listen and examine text says the footsteps stop when I stop, and that standing in the light is how such a one is met. Waiting brought the figure.
The disarmed figure hands the sword back 'hilt first, the way a teacher does.' It makes the fight feel like a lesson.
The wounded figure's lowering its head implies mercy, but I kept attacking with no sign that stopping was an option. It died anyway.
The sword stays in my hand and the rock no longer shows it. I could not tell whether that was meant to feel like a change.

wished: To spare the figure or speak to it.
To find the old man and some sign of what the final test is.
More explored map. I did not try the quicksand, the vegetation to the west or the northwest trail.

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
lines.why: The lantern description is warm and funny, and it sets a tone of weary familiarity.

lines.line: Instead it stoops, picks up your sword, and gives it back to you hilt first, the way a teacher does.
lines.why: This turns the combat into something tender and strange.

lines.line: the land of shadow is quiet in a way it was not before, as though something that had been waiting here a long time had stopped.
lines.why: A quiet, affecting close to the fight.

fun.why: The duel was surprising and graceful. The surrounding exploration was thin.

engagement.why: The footsteps hook pulled me forward, and the fight paid it off.

difficulty.why: The fight was simple to understand and self-correcting. I lost the sword repeatedly and the figure just returned it.

interestingness.why: The mirror-self idea and the teacher-like enemy are fresh against the usual combat.

prose.why: The descriptions are precise and have character, with the sword, the lantern and the footsteps as examples.
